title: add benchmark-lab edge-case profiling baselines and reporting pipeline
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We have a gap in our benchmark-lab coverage for low-frequency, worst-case inference patterns (very long prompt + many short completions, highly branching sampling, and KV-cache stress scenarios). These edge cases have historically caused regressions in batching logic and memory accounting. This PR adds representative workload runners for those edge cases, baseline profiles, and a reporting pipeline that aggregates daily runs into the telemetry store used by the benchmarking dashboard.

What this PR does: - Add edge_case_runner.py: a configurable runner that can generate synthetic workloads exercising long-prefix + short-complete patterns, high sampling branching, and KV cache churn. - Add profiling baselines YAMLs under profiling/baselines/edge_cases.yaml defining target P50/P95 latency, peak memory, and token throughput for supported GPU classes. - Add reporting pipeline config at pipelines/reporting/edge_case_pipeline.yaml which schedules nightly runs, uploads metrics to the benchmark telemetry service, and emits alerts when regressions happen. - Add lightweight dashboard and query snippets for console: observability/dashboards/edge-case-bench.json and docs updates with reproduction steps. - Add tests for the runner and CI workflow updates so nightly runs are validated in dry-run mode in CI.

Checklist: - [x] Add runners and baseline configs - [x] Wire reporting pipeline to telemetry ingestion API - [x] Add dashboard artifacts and docs - [x] Unit tests for runner core logic - [x] CI workflow that validates config and dry-run execution

Notes: The description intentionally keeps the runner deterministic by default; load variability is enabled via CLI flags. Reporting pipeline uses an incremental ingestion mode to avoid reprocessing. See linked Linear tasks for follow-ups on adding multi-variant comparison and automated anomaly detection.

Related: Linear ENG-1923 (edge-case coverage), ENG-1978 (reporting pipeline enhancements).

review_comments: Jordan Lee: Can you add more context on metric naming? We need P95_latency_ms vs p95_latency to keep consistent with dashboard queries.
Asha Patel: Updated baselines YAML and added explicit metric keys (p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, peak_memory_mb).
Priya Nair: Memory limits look tight on the a100-80gb profile; can we add a safety margin?
Asha Patel: Increased memory headroom by 10% for the a100-80gb target and documented rationale in the baseline file.
Ethan Wu: Found a flaky test in test_edge_runner when sampling_rate=0.8; suggested seeding RNG and adding a small tolerance for throughput assertion.
Asha Patel: Seeding RNG and relaxing throughput assertion by 3%; reran tests locally and in CI.
Jordan Lee: CI initially failed integration-tests due to missing telemetry credentials in the runner dry-run path. Please ensure dry-run doesn't require credentials.
Asha Patel: Fixed ingestion client to fall back to local file emitter in dry-run mode and added a CI secret placeholder for nightly runs.
ci_checks: integration-tests: originally failed (missing credentials) -> rerun: pass
merge_notes: Squash-merged after all reviewers approved. Small follow-ups (ENG-2032) planned to add multi-variant comparison and anomaly detection in the reporting pipeline.
release_notes: Add edge-case profiling baselines and nightly reporting pipeline for benchmark-lab. New runner enables long-prefix/short-completion, branching sampling, and KV-cache stress scenarios. Baselines and dashboards included.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: nightly reporting might produce noisy alerts until baselines mature. Mitigation: pipeline created with an initial 7-day stabilization window and alerts routed to the benchmark-lab Slack channel with a manual confirmation step before on-call pages.
testing_instructions: Run pytest tests/benchmark_lab/test_edge_runner.py and then run benchmark-lab/runners/edge_case_runner.py --dry-run --config benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/edge_cases.yaml. For nightly verification, check pipeline dry-run logs in CI and telemetry ingestion success in the benchmark telemetry UI.
notes_for_release: No breaking changes. This is additive to benchmark-lab and should not affect existing workloads. Nightly runs are opt-in until we enable alerts post-stabilization.
